sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:60

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:60:1
items.html:
The light of Tifferet, which remained in its place and whose taste did not change, etc.: Here he gives a reason for the expansion of the vessel of Keter down to the Chazeh [chest]. Likewise below he gives a reason for the expansion of the vessel of Bina down to Gevura, in order to give place to the reign of Netzah and Hod, and likewise the reason for the expansion of the vessel of Hesed, in order to give place to the reign of Yesod, see there. Now, there is no need at all for any of these reasons according to the words of the ARI in several places (in Etz Chaim, Gate 9, Chapter 4) and in Mavo Shearim, Gate 2, Part 2, Chapter 6, and these are his words there: “And when Tifferet died, and the light began to die and to depart from the first third down to the Chazeh, the general five Hassadim and Gevurot descended from the two Yesodot of the two Malchuts of the upper AVI, and their posterior finished falling entirely, and the posterior of the upper AVI was found sitting here below in this manner: the posterior of Aba sits in the right line, in the place where the Hesed of ZA had been, which is the second king, and the posterior of Ima in the place where the third king had been, which is the Gevura of ZA, as is known, for AVI were in the secret of lines, as above. And by force of these posteriors having fallen down to here, this is the phase of the new vessel that AVI made when they expanded down to here, and Hesed and Gevura afterward rose there. And that expansion is itself the phase of these posteriors that fell down to there … and the lights of Hesed and Gevura clothed in these two posteriors, and the lights of Netzah and Hod as well, except that all of them are above, in the place of Hesed and Gevura; understand this well.” End of quote. In the same way, the vessel of Keter was made from the phase of the posterior of NHY of Keter, which were flawed and descended below, as is written there.
Now, according to this, the matter of the expansion of the vessels of KHB into HGT is one and the same thing as the fall of the posterior of AVI and of the NHY of Keter, as the ARI says there. If so, there is no longer any question at all as to why the three lines of KHB expanded, and these reasons have no matter and no place whatsoever.
What is more, these reasons also contradict the words of the ARI cited above. For according to the reasons he writes here for the expansion of the lines — that it was in order to give place to the kings NHYM — it turns out that the line of Bina expanded before the line of Hochma, since NH reigned before Yesod, and therefore he says here that first the line of Bina expanded and afterward Hochma. But according to the truth, that they are the phase of the posterior that fell from AVI and from Keter, the line of Hochma expanded before the line of Bina, for the posterior of Hochma fell with the death of the vessel of Hesed, and the posterior of Ima fell with the death of the vessel of Gevura. Thus first the line of Hochma expanded to Hesed, and afterward the line of Bina to Gevura, which is the opposite of what he writes here. Perhaps these are two traditions from the ARI; and it is more correct that these reasons are from Rav Chaim Vital himself and are not at all from the words of the ARI.
Besides what has been said, it further follows from the above reasons that the vessels of the kings NH fell between the vessels of HGT, as he brings below. And this is hard to accept, for NHY with respect to HGT are as VAK with respect to GAR, and how could a vessel of VAK fall and dwell in the midst of the vessels of GAR, between Hesed and Gevura?
Now, it has been well explained in the words of the ARI in Mavo Shearim cited above that immediately upon the death of the upper third of Tifferet, when all the posterior of AVI finished falling and thereby became three new vessels — Hesed, Gevura and Tifferet — immediately the four lights of the four kings Daat, Hesed, Gevura and Tifferet rose there together. And the records of Daat and Tifferet clothed in the new vessel of Tifferet, the record of Hesed in the new vessel of Hesed, and likewise the record of Gevura in the vessel of Gevura.
